source_text: His definitionibus provocatae a nobis et revictae haereses omnes, sive quae posterae, sive quae coaetaneae apostolorum, dummodo diversae, sive generaliter, sive specialiter notatae ab eis, dummodo praedamnatae, audeant respondere et ipsae aliquas eiusmodi praescriptiones adversus nostram disciplinam. Si enim negant veritatem eius, debent probare illam quoque haeresin esse eadem forma revictam qua ipsae revincuntur, et ostendere simul ubinam quaerenda sit veritas quam apud illas non esse iam constat. Posterior nostra res non est, immo omnibus prior est, et hoc erit testimonium veritatis ubique occupantis principatum: apostolis ubique non damnatur, immo defenditur, hoc erit indicium proprietatis. Quam enim non damnant qui extraneam quamque damnarunt, suam ostendunt, ideoque et defendunt.
thought_title: The challenge to heretics to prove their own case
orientation: Tertullian has just shown that all heresies are late and already condemned; now he turns to the heretics and challenges them to answer with the same kind of legal objection against the church's discipline.
pass_a_gloss: All heresies, provoked by these definitions and refuted by us, whether the later ones or the ones contemporary with the apostles, provided they are different, whether noted generally or specifically by them, provided they were condemned beforehand, let them dare to answer and themselves bring some legal objections of this kind against our discipline. For if they deny the truth of it, they ought to prove that that too is a heresy refuted by the same form by which they themselves are refuted, and to show at the same time where the truth is to be sought, which it is already established is not among them. Our affair is not later, indeed it is prior to all, and this will be the testimony of the truth occupying the first place everywhere: by the apostles it is not condemned everywhere, indeed it is defended, this will be the proof of ownership. For the one which they do not condemn, they who condemned every foreign one, they show to be their own, and therefore they also defend it.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'legal objection' for praescriptio; the plural here refers to the same kind of legal objections Tertullian has been making.
The glossary requires 'discipline' for disciplina, meaning the ordered teaching and way of life of the church.
The glossary requires 'heresy' for haeresis, a faction choosing its own doctrine against the apostolic faith.
Renders the idea of priority and preeminence in time, matching the argument that the church's truth is prior to all heresies.
Captures the legal sense of proprietas as rightful possession, fitting the legal-objection framework of the treatise.
Renders extraneus as belonging to another, contrasting with what is one's own; the heretics condemned every foreign doctrine.

pass_b_english: All heresies have now been challenged and refuted by these definitions. Let them dare to answer, whether they arose after the apostles or in their own time, so long as they were different; whether the apostles marked them out generally or specifically, so long as they were condemned beforehand. Let them dare to bring legal objections of this same kind against our discipline.

If they deny that our discipline is the truth, they must prove that it too is a heresy, refuted by the same form of argument by which they themselves are refuted. They must also show where the truth is to be sought, since it is already established that it is not among them.

Our teaching is not later than theirs. Indeed, it is prior to all of them, and this will be the testimony of the truth that everywhere holds first place. Everywhere the apostles do not condemn it; indeed, they defend it. This will be the proof of ownership. For the doctrine they do not condemn, after condemning every foreign one, they show to be their own, and therefore they defend it.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening challenge as a direct summons to the heretics, broke the long first sentence into two natural sentences, made the pronouns and possessives explicit (our discipline, our teaching, the apostles), and restored the logical sequence of proof, ownership, and defense in the final paragraph.

notes.why: The intro explains 'legal objection' renders praescriptio, but the Latin term itself never appears in the body.
notes.fix: Use 'legal objection' consistently or include the Latin term at first use in the body.
